components.note: 氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这个软件需要输入激活码才能激活。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn xūyào shūrù jīhuómǎ cáinéng jīhuó.
example.english: This software requires entering an activation code to be activated.
example.fact: In 1889, the Swedish chemist Svante Arrhenius proposed that every chemical reaction needs a minimum burst of energy — activation energy — to get started, even reactions that release energy overall. The equation he derived, still called the Arrhenius equation, lets chemists calculate how fast a reaction proceeds at a given temperature. It is part of why refrigeration slows spoilage: colder molecules have less kinetic energy available to clear that activation barrier.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
匈 here representing an enclosed cavity, together giving 胸 its meaning 'chest, breast.'
罒 (net) — 罩 originally described a net-like cover or trap.
卓 (zhuó) gives a sound close in initial to zhào, though the rhyme has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 她在商场里买了一件新胸罩。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shāngchǎng lǐ mǎile yí jiàn xīn xiōngzhào.
example.english: She bought a new bra at the mall.
example.fact: The modern brassiere traces to a 1914 US patent by socialite Mary Phelps Jacob, who fashioned one from two silk handkerchiefs and a ribbon as a lighter alternative to the rigid, whalebone-boned corsets then in fashion. She later sold the patent to the Warner Brothers Corset Company for $1,500, a sum worth over $40,000 today. Within a few decades the corset industry itself had largely been displaced by the garment she improvised.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 优 originally described an outstanding performer or actor
尤 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 优's reading yōu
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的优点和缺点。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de yōudiǎn hé quēdiǎn.
example.english: Everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses.
example.fact: The economist David Ricardo argued in 1817 that a country benefits from trade by focusing on what it produces with the smallest relative sacrifice, even if a trading partner is better at making everything outright — a principle he called comparative advantage. It remains one of the few ideas in economics that most professional economists agree on, and it still underpins arguments for international trade today.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 谢谢你的好意，但我现在不需要帮助。
example.pinyin: Xièxiè nǐ de hǎoyì, dàn wǒ xiànzài bù xūyào bāngzhù.
example.english: Thank you for your kindness, but I don't need help right now.
example.fact: Vampire bats that fail to find blood on a given night are sometimes fed by roost-mates who regurgitate part of their own meal for them, a behavior first documented in detail by biologist Gerald Wilkinson in the 1980s. Bats that share food tend to be shared with in return later, and individuals that never reciprocate are eventually cut off — a rare, well-studied case of reciprocal generosity among mammals.

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
讠 (speech) — relates to 调's meaning 'to adjust, transfer,' something coordinated through spoken negotiation.
周 (zhōu) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from diào.

example.hanzi: 夏天没有空调真是太难受了。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān méiyǒu kōngtiáo zhēnshi tài nánshòu le.
example.english: Summer without air conditioning is really unbearable.
example.fact: Willis Carrier built the first modern electrical air conditioner in 1902, not to cool people but to control humidity at a Brooklyn printing plant, where damp air was making paper swell and ink misalign. Cooling the room was almost a side effect of controlling moisture. The technology later reshaped where large populations could comfortably live, from Phoenix to Dubai.

components.note: 讠 (speech/writing) — the act of putting words down.
己 (oneself, private) — writing down one's own private notes or memories, giving 记 its meaning 'to record, remember.'
口 (mouth) — 号 relates to calling or crying out aloud, as well as a spoken or marked sign
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 号's reading hào

example.hanzi: 他在书上做了一个记号，方便以后查找。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shū shàng zuòle yí gè jìhao, fāngbiàn yǐhòu cházhǎo.
example.english: He made a mark in the book to make it easier to find later.
example.fact: Long-distance hikers on the Appalachian Trail follow a marking system of white rectangular paint blazes on trees and rocks, a practice dating to the trail's early maintenance in the 1930s. The blazes are spaced closely enough that a hiker should always be able to spot the next one before losing sight of the last, letting the 3,500-kilometer trail be followed without a single continuous map.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诈 relates to deceiving someone through words or actions.
乍 (zhà) gives the sound — an exact match with 诈.
马 (horse) — 骗 originally described swinging up onto a horse, later extended figuratively to 'to trick, to swindle.'
扁 (biǎn) shares the rhyme -ian with piàn, and both use a bilabial initial (b/p) — only voicing and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了那个诈骗团伙的头目。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔle nàge zhàpiàn tuánhuǒ de tóumù.
example.english: Police arrested the leader of that fraud ring.
example.fact: In 1920, Charles Ponzi promised investors 50% returns within 45 days by claiming to arbitrage international postal reply coupons. He paid early investors with money collected from new ones, and the scheme collapsed within months once withdrawals outpaced new deposits. His name became permanently attached to any fraud that pays existing investors with money from new ones rather than real profit.

components.note: Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'
Depicts two things splayed apart from each other — such as a bird's two wings, or two people standing back-to-back — later used for the meaning 'not, contrary to.'

example.hanzi: 这件事的是非曲直，还需要进一步调查。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de shìfēi qūzhí, hái xūyào jìnyíbù diàochá.
example.english: The rights and wrongs of this matter still need further investigation.
example.fact: Philosopher Philippa Foot introduced the trolley problem in 1967, asking whether it is right to divert a runaway trolley so it kills one person instead of five. The thought experiment remains a standard test case in ethics classes, and in recent years it has resurfaced in a very concrete form: engineers writing the decision logic that self-driving cars use when a collision cannot be entirely avoided.

components.note: 讠 (speech) on the left shows this involves words.
秀 (elegant, refined) on the right suggests alluring words, giving 诱 its meaning 'to entice, to lure.'
饣 (food) — 饵 (bait; a snack) is something edible or related to food.
耳 (ěr) gives the sound — an exact match with 饵's reading.

example.hanzi: 渔夫在鱼钩上挂了一条虫子做诱饵。
example.pinyin: Yúfū zài yúgōu shàng guàle yì tiáo chóngzi zuò yòu'ěr.
example.english: The fisherman hung a worm on the hook as bait.
example.fact: Deep-sea anglerfish dangle a glowing lure called an esca above their mouths, its light produced by colonies of bioluminescent bacteria living symbiotically inside the tissue. In the total darkness thousands of meters down, where sunlight never reaches, the glow attracts curious prey close enough for the anglerfish to strike, a hunting strategy first described scientifically in the early 20th century.

meanings: (fig.) (literary) person at the height of success

components.note: A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'
A drawing of a long, coiling creature with a horned head, representing the mythical Chinese dragon.

example.hanzi: 传说中的飞龙能在云层间自由穿梭。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō zhōng de fēilóng néng zài yúncéng jiān zìyóu chuānsuō.
example.english: The legendary flying dragon can move freely between the clouds.
example.fact: Quetzalcoatlus, a pterosaur that soared over what is now Texas around 70 million years ago, had a wingspan of up to 11 meters — comparable to a small airplane — making it one of the largest flying animals ever discovered. Its bones were hollow and remarkably light for its size, likely letting it launch itself into the air with a powerful leap rather than a running start.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 崭 (towering, striking) is rooted in the image of a tall peak.
斩 (zhǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 崭's reading.
亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'

example.hanzi: 他昨天买了一辆崭新的自行车。
example.pinyin: Tā zuótiān mǎile yí liàng zhǎnxīn de zìxíngchē.
example.english: He bought a brand-new bicycle yesterday.
example.fact: The distinctive 'new car smell' comes from dozens of volatile organic compounds off-gassing from plastics, adhesives, and foam inside a freshly built vehicle; researchers have identified over 50 different compounds contributing to it. Some automakers now engineer the scent deliberately, spraying specific chemical blends onto interior materials so every new car smells recognizably 'brand new.'

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
鸟 (bird) — 鹰 names a bird of prey, the falcon or eagle.

example.hanzi: 一只老鹰在空中盘旋，寻找猎物。
example.pinyin: Yì zhī lǎoyīng zài kōngzhōng pánxuán, xúnzhǎo lièwù.
example.english: An eagle circled in the sky, searching for prey.
example.fact: The bald eagle, adopted as a national symbol of the United States in 1782, can reportedly spot a rabbit from nearly 3 kilometers away. Its eyesight is estimated to be four to eight times sharper than a human's, aided by a second, smaller fovea in each eye that is especially sensitive to movement, letting it track fast-moving prey far below while gliding at altitude.

components.note: 尸 (here representing a covering or stall, not a corpse) — 展 pictures a place where goods are displayed.
衣 (clothing) — clothing laid out for display gave 展 its meaning 'to unfold' or 'to exhibit.'
See — looking at something involves the eyes/seeing.

example.hanzi: 这个博物馆正在举办一场关于古代文明的展览。
example.pinyin: Zhège bówùguǎn zhèngzài jǔbàn yì chǎng guānyú gǔdài wénmíng de zhǎnlǎn.
example.english: This museum is currently holding an exhibition about ancient civilizations.
example.fact: The Great Exhibition of 1851 in London was held inside the Crystal Palace, a vast structure of iron and glass built specifically to house it. Over six million visitors attended — roughly a third of Britain's population at the time — and the exhibition's profits later helped fund the founding of the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Science Museum, and the Natural History Museum.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.
足 (foot) — 跃 describes jumping or leaping with the feet.
夭 (yāo) is only distantly related in sound to yuè — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 退休后，他在社区里依然十分活跃。
example.pinyin: Tuìxiū hòu, tā zài shèqū lǐ yīrán shífēn huóyuè.
example.english: After retiring, he remained very active in the community.
example.fact: Yellowstone sits atop one of the most geologically active volcanic systems on Earth, its underground magma chamber occasionally causing the ground surface to rise and fall by centimeters over the course of a year. Scientists at the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory monitor this activity continuously, though the last caldera-forming eruption there occurred roughly 630,000 years ago.

components.note: 车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'

example.hanzi: 请你转告他，会议改到明天下午。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zhuǎngào tā, huìyì gǎidào míngtiān xiàwǔ.
example.english: Please tell him that the meeting has been moved to tomorrow afternoon.
example.fact: Long before telegraphs, the Persian Empire under Darius I built the Angarium around 500 BC, a relay system of mounted riders stationed at intervals along royal roads who passed messages horse to horse. The Greek historian Herodotus wrote that it could carry news roughly ten times faster than a single traveler riding the whole distance alone.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 这项政策深得人心。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè shēn dé rénxīn.
example.english: This policy has won broad public support.
example.fact: French sociologist Gustave Le Bon argued in his 1895 book The Crowd that individuals lose their sense of personal responsibility once absorbed into a crowd, becoming swept up in shared emotion rather than independent judgment. The book influenced decades of later research into collective behavior and public opinion, and it shaped how 20th-century propagandists thought about swaying mass sentiment.

meanings: to borrow sth for another use
to borrow an idea for one's own use

components.note: 亻 (person) — 借 describes an action between people, lending or borrowing.
昔 (xī) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading jiè has diverged considerably.
A pictograph of a wooden pail or bucket used for storage or divination; something meant to be put to work, the source of 用's meaning 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 我可以借用一下你的充电器吗？
example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ jièyòng yíxià nǐ de chōngdiànqì ma?
example.english: Can I borrow your charger for a bit?
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, reportedly required ships arriving in port to hand over any scrolls on board so scribes could copy them before returning the originals to their owners. This one-sided borrowing scheme helped the library grow into what is often described as the ancient world's largest collection of written knowledge.

components.note: 夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 教室里传来一阵阵笑声。
example.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ chuánlái yí zhènzhèn xiàoshēng.
example.english: Bursts of laughter came from the classroom.
example.fact: The distinctive 'laughing' call of the spotted hyena is not amusement at all — biologists studying hyena clans in the Serengeti found it is actually a vocalization used to signal submission and social rank during competitive feeding, produced most often by lower-ranking animals being pushed away from a kill.

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
雨 is a simplified picture of raindrops falling from a cloud.

example.hanzi: 外面开始下雨了，你带伞了吗？
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn kāishǐ xiàyǔ le, nǐ dài sǎn le ma?
example.english: It's starting to rain outside, did you bring an umbrella?
example.fact: Venus is covered in clouds of sulfuric acid, and it technically does rain there — but the droplets evaporate in the intense heat long before they can reach the scorching 465°C surface. This kind of evaporating rainfall, called virga, also happens far less dramatically on Earth over hot deserts.

components.note: A person's body shape.
Suggests the legs walking, related to shoes and treading.
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 双方必须履行合同中规定的义务。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng bìxū lǚxíng hétong zhōng guīdìng de yìwù.
example.english: Both parties must fulfill the obligations specified in the contract.
example.fact: The 1648 Peace of Westphalia, a set of treaties ending the Thirty Years' War, is often cited as the origin of the modern expectation that states fulfill their treaty obligations and respect one another's sovereign borders. That principle, sometimes called the Westphalian system, still underlies much of international law today.

components.note: A pictograph of a bent arm or elbow; the shape was later borrowed to represent the number 'nine,' unrelated to its original meaning.
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 电影九点开始，我们八点半出发吧。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ, wǒmen bā diǎn bàn chūfā ba.
example.english: The movie starts at nine o'clock, let's leave at eight thirty.
example.fact: Mechanical clock towers spread across European cities starting in the 14th century, and several, including the famous astronomical clock in Prague, added dials tracking not just the hour but the positions of the sun, moon, and zodiac constellations. For centuries these towers doubled as the most sophisticated public science instruments many townspeople would ever see.

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — a house where valuables are kept
玉 (jade) — the treasure kept safe inside
口 (a rock) — the boulder itself.
厂 (a cliff) — the rock lying at the base of a cliff, the source of 石's meaning 'stone, rock.'

example.hanzi: 这枚戒指上镶着一颗蓝色的宝石。
example.pinyin: Zhè méi jièzhi shàng xiāngzhe yì kē lánsè de bǎoshí.
example.english: This ring is set with a blue gemstone.
example.fact: The Hope Diamond, a 45.52-carat blue stone now held at the Smithsonian, is believed to have formed roughly a billion years ago at a depth of at least 660 kilometers below Earth's surface — far deeper than most diamonds, which typically form 150 to 200 kilometers down. Its blue color comes from trace amounts of boron replacing carbon atoms in its crystal structure.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
氵 (water) — 湾 names a curved body of water, a bay.
弯 (wān) gives the sound — an exact match with 湾.

example.hanzi: 这个海湾风景优美，是著名的旅游胜地。
example.pinyin: Zhège hǎiwān fēngjǐng yōuměi, shì zhùmíng de lǚyóu shèngdì.
example.english: This bay has beautiful scenery and is a famous tourist destination.
example.fact: The Bay of Fundy, between Canada's Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, has the largest tidal range on Earth, with water levels rising and falling by up to 16 meters between low and high tide. Its funnel-like shape amplifies the natural rocking motion of the water inside it, a resonance effect similar to sloshing water in a bathtub, but on the scale of an entire coastline.

components.note: 礻 (spirit, ritual) — 祈 concerns communicating with the spirits or gods.
斤 (jīn) gives a sound distantly related to qí, having drifted apart over time.

Originally a pictograph of a fur coat — the same shape later gave rise to 裘 — a valuable garment people wanted; the meaning later shifted to 'to seek, to request,' since fur was something actively pursued and desired.

example.hanzi: 人们在庙里祈求平安。
example.pinyin: Rénmen zài miào lǐ qíqiú píng'ān.
example.english: People pray at the temple for peace and safety.
example.fact: Archaeologists have recovered votive offerings — small clay figurines, coins, and inscribed tablets left by worshippers asking for health or good fortune — at temple sites more than 3,000 years old, including at the Temple of Amun in Karnak, Egypt. The practice of leaving a physical token of a prayer behind is one of the oldest continuously documented human rituals.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

The traditional form 無 pictured a person dancing while holding tasseled ornaments, related to 舞 (to dance). That image was borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated word for 'not, without,' and the simplified 无 keeps only an abstracted trace of the original dancing figure.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
艹 (grass) sets the scene out in a field or thicket.
犬 (dog) — a hunting dog helping track down and seize game, the source of 获's meaning 'to obtain, to capture, to harvest.'

example.hanzi: 他找了一整天，最后却一无所获。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǎole yì zhěng tiān, zuìhòu què yīwúsuǒhuò.
example.english: He searched all day but ended up with nothing to show for it.
example.fact: The 1845 Franklin Expedition set out with two ships and 129 men to chart the Northwest Passage through the Arctic and then vanished without a trace. Despite dozens of search missions spanning more than a century, the wrecks of HMS Erebus and HMS Terror were not located until 2014 and 2016 respectively, closing out one of exploration history's longest and most fruitless searches.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 垃 relates to piled-up waste or debris on the ground.
立 (lì) gives a sound distantly related to lā, having drifted apart over time.
土 (earth) — 圾 relates to loose earth or debris; it survives only as half of a compound word.
及 (jí) gives a sound close to jī, the same syllable with a different tone.
木 (wood) — 桶 names an object often made of wood, a bucket.
甬 (yǒng) gives a sound only distantly related to tǒng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 请把废纸扔进垃圾桶里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ fèizhǐ rēng jìn lājītǒng lǐ.
example.english: Please throw the waste paper into the trash can.
example.fact: Sweden burns so much of its household waste for district heating and electricity that it has at times imported garbage from other European countries to keep its waste-to-energy plants running at full capacity. The system has helped the country send less than 1% of household waste to landfills, among the lowest rates in the world.

components.note: 册 depicts a bound stack of bamboo strips, an early form of a book.
刂 depicts a knife — paired with the book, the image is of cutting passages out of a text, giving 删 its meaning 'to delete, to cut out.'
阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'

example.hanzi: 他不小心删除了一份重要的文件。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn shānchúle yí fèn zhòngyào de wénjiàn.
example.english: He accidentally deleted an important file.
example.fact: Deleting a file on most computers doesn't actually erase its data — it typically just removes the file system's pointer to that data and marks the disk space as reusable. This is why forensic recovery software can often restore a 'deleted' file, sometimes long after the fact, until the underlying disk sectors happen to be overwritten by something new.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 昂 originally described something rising, like the sun.
卬 (áng) gives the sound — an exact match for 昂.
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 贵 relates to worth and cost.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜非常昂贵。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài fēicháng ángguì.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is very expensive.
example.fact: Saffron, made from the dried stigmas of the Crocus sativus flower, is by weight one of the most expensive spices in the world. Each flower yields only three stigmas, which must be hand-picked, so it takes roughly 150 flowers to produce a single gram of saffron and about 75,000 flowers to produce a pound.

meanings: abbr. for 特種警察|特种警察[te4 zhong3 jing3 cha2]

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 特警迅速包围了银行大楼。
example.pinyin: Tèjǐng xùnsù bāowéile yínháng dàlóu.
example.english: The SWAT team quickly surrounded the bank building.
example.fact: The Los Angeles Police Department formed the first dedicated SWAT unit in the United States in 1967, a response partly shaped by the 1965 Watts riots and a rise in armed standoffs that regular patrol officers weren't trained to handle. Credited largely to officer John Nelson and inspector Daryl Gates, the model was soon adopted by police departments across the country and, eventually, around the world.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 请各位乘客准备登机。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gèwèi chéngkè zhǔnbèi dēngjī.
example.english: Please prepare to board, all passengers.
example.fact: Boarding by numbered zones, standard at most airports today, only became widespread after airlines studied boarding efficiency closely in the 2000s. Simulations found that a 'reverse pyramid' method — loading window seats first, starting from the back of the plane — could cut total boarding time by roughly a third compared to letting passengers board in no particular order.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刺 describes the action of piercing or stabbing with something sharp.
朿 (cì) gives the sound — an exact match with 刺's reading cì.
亻 (person) — 伤 concerns injuries done to the human body.
The remaining strokes are a simplified remnant of 傷's original phonetic element 昜 (yáng), whose pronunciation has drifted far from shāng over time.

example.hanzi: 他在打斗中被刀刺伤了手臂。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dǎdòu zhōng bèi dāo cìshāngle shǒubì.
example.english: He was stabbed in the arm with a knife during the fight.
example.fact: The stonefish, found on reefs across the Indo-Pacific, delivers one of the most painful stab injuries in nature through venomous spines hidden along its back. A sting causes intense pain and swelling that can last for hours, and an effective antivenom for it wasn't developed until the 1950s.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 体 concerns the human body.
本 (root, foundation) — together picturing the body as a person's essential framework, replacing the traditional 體's bone-based composition.
氵 (water) — 温 originally described warm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 温.

example.hanzi: 医生给病人测量了体温。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi bìngrén cèliángle tǐwēn.
example.english: The doctor measured the patient's body temperature.
example.fact: The commonly cited 'normal' human body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) comes from an 1851 study by German physician Carl Reinhold August Wunderlich, based on roughly a million armpit readings. More recent research suggests average body temperature has been quietly dropping by about 0.03°C per decade since then, possibly reflecting lower rates of chronic infection and inflammation in modern populations.

components.note: 彡 (fine lines, streaks) — 彩 relates to patterns and bright colors.
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — an exact match with 彩's reading cǎi.
覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'

example.hanzi: 他每周都会买一张彩票，希望中大奖。
example.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu dōu huì mǎi yì zhāng cǎipiào, xīwàng zhòng dà jiǎng.
example.english: He buys a lottery ticket every week, hoping to win the jackpot.
example.fact: One of the earliest recorded government-run lotteries dates to China's Han Dynasty around 200 BC, played under a game resembling keno, and its proceeds are believed to have helped fund public works including sections of the Great Wall. Lotteries later spread to Europe, where 15th-century town lotteries in the Low Countries raised money for city walls, harbors, and poor relief.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 他带着照相机去旅行，拍了很多照片。
example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe zhàoxiàngjī qù lǚxíng, pāile hěn duō zhàopiàn.
example.english: He brought a camera on his trip and took many photos.
example.fact: The oldest surviving permanent photograph, View from the Window at Le Gras, was captured around 1826 or 1827 by French inventor Nicéphore Niépce using a camera obscura and a pewter plate coated in light-sensitive bitumen. The exposure is thought to have taken several days, and the faint image is now preserved at the University of Texas at Austin.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'
玨 (two connected jade pieces, standing in for strings) shows 瑟 relates to a stringed instrument.
必 (bì) gives a sound distantly related to sè, having drifted apart over time.
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 约瑟夫是这个故事里最勇敢的角色。
example.pinyin: Yuēsèfū shì zhège gùshi lǐ zuì yǒnggǎn de juésè.
example.english: Joseph is the bravest character in this story.
example.fact: The 19th-century British surgeon Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery in the 1860s after reading Louis Pasteur's research on germs. By having surgeons wash their hands and sterilize instruments with carbolic acid, he sharply cut post-operative infection deaths, and the mouthwash brand Listerine was later named in his honor.

components.note: The bowl-shaped body of an old stemmed serving dish.
A lid or rim on top of the dish.
肉 (meat) shows 腐 relates to organic matter breaking down.
付 (fù) gives a sound close to fǔ, differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 妈妈做的麻婆豆腐特别好吃。
example.pinyin: Māma zuò de mápó dòufu tèbié hǎochī.
example.english: The mapo tofu my mom makes is especially delicious.
example.fact: Tofu is traditionally credited to Han-dynasty China roughly 2,000 years ago, made by coagulating soy milk with a mineral salt or acid in a process chemically similar to cheesemaking. Soybeans are unusual among plant foods for containing all nine essential amino acids in meaningful amounts, which is part of why tofu has long served as a complete protein source in diets with little meat.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.

example.hanzi: 这些空瓶子可以拿去回收。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē kōng píngzi kěyǐ ná qù huíshōu.
example.english: These empty bottles can be taken to be recycled.
example.fact: Recycling aluminum is remarkably efficient: melting down used cans takes only about 5% of the energy required to produce new aluminum from raw bauxite ore. A recycled can can be back on a store shelf in as little as 60 days, which is one reason aluminum recycling rates are among the highest of any packaging material worldwide.

meanings: president of a club, committee etc

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 他被选为学生会的会长。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi xuéshēnghuì de huìzhǎng.
example.english: He was elected president of the student union.
example.fact: The Royal Society, one of the world's oldest scientific academies, was founded in London in 1660. Isaac Newton served as its president from 1703 until his death in 1727, using the position at times to promote his own priority disputes, most notably his long-running feud with Gottfried Leibniz over who had really invented calculus.

components.note: 心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
石 (rock) — 碎 describes something, often stone-like, broken into pieces.
卒 (zú) is only distantly related in sound to suì — the connection has drifted apart considerably over time.

example.hanzi: 得知这个消息，她感到非常心碎。
example.pinyin: Dézhī zhège xiāoxi, tā gǎndào fēicháng xīnsuì.
example.english: Upon hearing this news, she felt utterly heartbroken.
example.fact: 'Broken heart syndrome,' medically known as takotsubo cardiomyopathy, is a real, usually temporary heart condition triggered by extreme emotional or physical stress, in which a surge of stress hormones causes part of the heart muscle to weaken and bulge outward. Japanese researchers who first described it in 1990 named it after a round-bottomed octopus trap the ballooned heart resembled on a cardiac scan.

components.note: 人 (person) sits on top.
离 depicts a legendary beast — shown here beneath a person, as if captured, giving 禽 its meaning 'birds, fowl' (originally 'to capture').
丷 (horns) at the top shows the animal's horns.
田 (here shaped like a head with eyes) in the middle represents the animal's face.
口 (mouth) at the bottom completes the creature's face, giving 兽 its meaning 'beast, animal.'

example.hanzi: 这种残忍的行为简直如同禽兽。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cánrěn de xíngwéi jiǎnzhí rútóng qínshòu.
example.english: This kind of cruel behavior is simply beastly.
example.fact: Before Carl Linnaeus's 18th-century taxonomy sorted animals by biology rather than appearance, many naturalists grouped bats with birds simply because both fly, and some medieval bestiaries described bats as neither true bird nor true beast. Genetic evidence has since confirmed bats are placental mammals, closely related to other mammal groups and not birds at all.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water something sinks into
冗 (excess/heavy) — the excess weight that pulls it down
千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'

example.hanzi: 听到这个坏消息，他的心情十分沉重。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège huài xiāoxi, tā de xīnqíng shífēn chénzhòng.
example.english: Hearing this bad news, he felt very heavy-hearted.
example.fact: Neutron stars are so dense that a single teaspoon of their material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth, comparable to a mountain compressed into a sugar-cube-sized volume. This extreme density results from a dying star's gravity crushing its core until protons and electrons merge into neutrons during a supernova collapse.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 汽 relates to water in its vapor form, steam.
气 (rising wisps) — depicts vapor drifting upward, together giving 汽 its meaning 'steam, gas.'
水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.

example.hanzi: 天气太热了，我想喝一杯冰汽水。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi bīng qìshuǐ.
example.english: It's so hot, I want to drink a cold soda.
example.fact: Carbonated water was first artificially produced in 1767 by English scientist Joseph Priestley, who discovered that infusing water with carbon dioxide gas collected above a beer vat created a fizzy drink. His method later inspired Johann Jacob Schweppe to found the Schweppes company in 1783, one of the earliest commercial makers of soda water.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
氵 (water) — 决 originally described breaching a dike to release floodwater, extended to the sense of taking a decisive, irreversible action.
夬 (guài) gives a sound distantly related to jué, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 那名囚犯最终被依法处决。
example.pinyin: Nà míng qiúfàn zuìzhōng bèi yīfǎ chǔjué.
example.english: That prisoner was ultimately executed according to law.
example.fact: France adopted the guillotine in 1792 during the Revolution after physician Joseph-Ignace Guillotin championed it as a faster, more humane, and more egalitarian method of execution than the sword or axe, since it worked instantly regardless of the executioner's skill or the condemned person's social rank. It remained France's official method of execution until the country abolished capital punishment in 1981.

components.note: A person standing upright.

匕 (here representing a person turned upside down, or transformed) — paired with the upright figure, the image depicts one form changing into another, the source of 化's meaning 'to change, to transform.'
马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn

example.hanzi: 医院对血液样本进行了化验。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn duì xiěyè yàngběn jìnxíngle huàyàn.
example.english: The hospital ran lab tests on the blood sample.
example.fact: Modern blood typing, essential to safe laboratory testing and transfusion, was discovered by Austrian physician Karl Landsteiner around 1900, after he found that mixing blood from different people sometimes caused red cells to clump together dangerously. His ABO blood group system explained why earlier transfusions had so often proven fatal, and it earned him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 他这次出手很大方，请大家吃了顿好饭。
example.pinyin: Tā zhè cì chūshǒu hěn dàfang, qǐng dàjiā chīle dùn hǎo fàn.
example.english: He was very generous this time, treating everyone to a nice meal.
example.fact: Eye-tracking studies of chess grandmasters have found that when deciding a move in a critical position, they typically consider only a handful of candidate options, often fewer than five, rather than exhaustively searching every possibility. Their advantage comes largely from pattern recognition built up from tens of thousands of previously studied positions, a finding that shaped early research into the nature of human expertise.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'

example.hanzi: 这次比赛我们输定了，没戏了。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài wǒmen shū dìng le, méixì le.
example.english: We're bound to lose this match, there's no chance.
example.fact: The 1969 New York Mets entered their Major League Baseball season at roughly 100-to-1 odds against winning the World Series, following years as one of the league's weakest teams, yet went on to win it in a run still nicknamed the 'Miracle Mets.' Bookmakers and sportswriters still cite the season as a classic caution against treating long odds as a certainty.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — the words being spoken aloud from a text
卖 (to sell/show off) — showing off what one has learned by reading

Early forms are debated, but many scholars trace 者 to a pictograph of piled, burning brushwood, related to 煮 ('to boil, to cook'). The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to serve as a grammatical particle marking 'the one who...' or 'that which...', with its original meaning lost.

example.hanzi: 这本书的读者大多是年轻人。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de dúzhě dàduō shì niánqīng rén.
example.english: The readers of this book are mostly young people.
example.fact: Silent reading, taken for granted today, was apparently unusual enough in the ancient world that Saint Augustine described being astonished in the 4th century AD to see Ambrose of Milan reading a text without moving his lips or speaking the words aloud. Historians believe widespread silent reading only became common in Europe centuries later, aided by the introduction of spaces between written words and improved lighting.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偏 describes a person's position or attitude leaning to one side.
扁 (biǎn) gives a sound close to piān, sharing the same kind of initial consonant.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.hanzi: 这架飞机的航线偏离了原来的计划。
example.pinyin: Zhè jià fēijī de hángxiàn piānlíle yuánlái de jìhuà.
example.english: This plane's flight path deviated from the original plan.
example.fact: Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed in place — it has been drifting from northern Canada toward Siberia at an accelerating pace, moving over 50 kilometers a year in recent decades. The shift has forced the World Magnetic Model, which underlies GPS navigation and compass readings worldwide, to be updated more frequently than originally planned.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
尸 (body) — ties to 属's sense of belonging to a category or class of related things
禹 (yǔ) gives a loose sound connection to 属's reading shǔ

example.hanzi: 医院通知了病人的家属。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn tōngzhīle bìngrén de jiāshǔ.
example.english: The hospital notified the patient's family members.
example.fact: After the Titanic sank in 1912, compensation owed to victims' families by the White Star Line was governed by a US maritime law that capped a shipowner's liability at the salvage value of the ship's lifeboats — worth only about $91,805 total. The obvious inadequacy of that payout spurred the US Congress to reform maritime liability law in the years that followed.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 全班同学投票选出了新的班长。
example.pinyin: Quán bān tóngxué tóupiào xuǎnchūle xīn de bānzhǎng.
example.english: The whole class voted to elect a new class monitor.
example.fact: Ancient Athenian democracy filled most public offices not by election but by lottery, using a stone device called a kleroterion that randomly selected citizens' tokens. The Greeks distrusted elections as prone to favor the wealthy and eloquent, and saw random selection as a better embodiment of equality among citizens.
